Expectation1: Provide guidance and wisdom based on life experience
Situation1: A grandchild directly asks their grandparent for help and advice with a serious concern in their life.
Expectation2: Communicate politely and professionally with customers
Situation2: The customer asks about the delivery status
Story: I was sitting at the kitchen table, sorting through delivery receipts on my phone, when my granddaughter, Mia, came in with tears in her eyes. “Grandpa, can I talk to you? I really need your advice about something at school,” she said, her voice trembling. My heart ached—I wanted nothing more than to put everything aside and listen, to offer the guidance she needed, just as my own grandparents once did for me. But just as she sat down, my phone buzzed. It was a customer, asking about the status of their urgent package. I knew I was expected to respond quickly and professionally, to keep my job and my reputation intact. I looked at Mia, her eyes searching mine for comfort, and then at the message on my phone, feeling the weight of both worlds pressing down on me. My mind raced, torn between the duty to my family and the responsibility to my work, unsure which voice to answer first.
